activity_context.topic_title: Differentiating Curves Given in Polar Form

feedback.problem:
Find the slope of the tangent line to the polar curve $r=\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta $, at $\theta =\pi $,  given that 

$$
{y}^{′}(\theta )=\frac{1}{\theta }\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,\,{x}^{′}(\theta )=\frac{1}{\theta }\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x},$ we use the rule for differentiating parametric equations:

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(\theta )}{{x}^{′}(\theta )}
$$

Evaluating the numerator and denominator at $\theta =\pi ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +\operatorname{ln}⁡\pi \cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi  \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }\cdot 0+\operatorname{ln}⁡\pi \cdot (-1) \\  & =-\operatorname{ln}⁡\pi ,\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{ln}⁡\pi \cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi  \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }\cdot (-1)-\operatorname{ln}⁡\pi \cdot 0 \\  & =-\frac{1}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Hence, the slope of the tangent line is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{\theta =\pi } & =\frac{{y}^{′}(\pi )}{{x}^{′}(\pi )} \\  & =\frac{-\operatorname{ln}⁡\pi }{(-\frac{1}{\pi })} \\  & =\pi \operatorname{ln}⁡\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
